Both give me a safety net, and either would keep me from losing something by accident.

For deleting, though, I lean toward version A — asking me to confirm before it's gone. Since this is the permanent removal that also takes the note, labels, and read-later status with it, I'd rather be stopped and asked "are you sure?" up front than have it vanish and then hunt for an undo before it slips away. An undo banner is friendly, but if I look away or it disappears, the bookmark's gone for good. A quick confirm makes the permanence feel deliberate, which fits how serious this action is. So let's go with A.

And yes, your assumption is right — deleting should take everything attached to that bookmark with it. That's exactly why it deserves the guard.

I should mention, since it's closely related: this permanent delete is the right thing to have, but it's a bit heavy-handed as my *only* way to get something out of the way. Often I don't want a link gone forever — I just want it out of my main list without losing it. So I'd expect there to also be a gentler option alongside delete, for setting something aside in a way I can undo later. Not asking you to build it this second — just flagging that permanent delete shouldn't be the only tool for tidying up.
